resources.name: BannerClick
quotes: In early 2023, Rasaii et al. [51] presented BannerClick, a tool which can automatically detect and interact (i.e., accept and reject) with cookie banners with an accuracy of 99% and 96%, respectively.
Therefore, in this work we extend BannerClick to specifically detect these special types of cookie banners, i.e., cookiewalls.
We release our modified version of BannerClick as open-source software [50].
references: Ali Rasaii, Shivani Singh, Devashish Gosain, and Oliver Gasser. 2023. Exploring the Cookieverse: A Multi-Perspective Analysis of Web Cookies. In Proceedings of the 2023 Passive and Active Measurement Conference. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-28486-1_26
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The authors extended BannerClick to detect cookiewalls and used this modified version for their large-scale measurement study.

resources.name: OpenWPM
quotes: BannerClick is built on top of OpenWPM [21] and Selenium [58]
Although OpenWPM has mechanisms to mitigate bot detection, it is impossible to completely circumvent bot detection.
references: Steven Englehardt and Arvind Narayanan. 2016. Online tracking: A 1-million-site measurement and analysis. In Proceedings of the 2016 ACM SIGSAC conference on computer and communications security. 1388–1401.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The authors used OpenWPM as the underlying framework for BannerClick and relied on its bot detection mitigation mechanisms.

resources.name: Analysis scripts and raw data for Cookiewall measurements
quotes: we release... our analysis code and data [49] at bannerclick.github.io
Finally, we publish tools, data, and code to foster reproducibility and further studies.
references: Ali Rasaii. 2023. Analysis scripts and raw data for Cookiewall measurements . https://doi.org/10.17617/3.TREBZR.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The paper introduces and releases this dataset and the associated analysis code as a byproduct of the study to foster reproducibility.

resources.name: KU Leuven|Tranco
quotes: We use Google’s Chrome User Experience Report (CrUX) [10] for target selection, as it was shown to be a more realistic toplist [54] compared to Alexa [3] or Tranco [38].
references: Victor Le Pochat, Tom Van Goethem, Samaneh Tajalizadehkhoob, Maciej Korczyński, and Wouter Joosen. 2019. Tranco: A Research-Oriented Top Sites Ranking Hardened Against Manipulation. In Proceedings of the 26th Annual Network and Distributed System Security Symposium. Internet Society, 1–15.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: Tranco is mentioned as a point of comparison for the target selection process, but was not used to select the websites for the study.
